title: Round 3 c: the arena's hole never closes, the descent dives down it and climbs back out of it, and the cave's flares stick where they first touch rock
context: Owner, 2026-10-26, notes 4, 6 and 7: the sinkhole of sector 9 does not close, it is the Cave's entrance; flares stick to the surface they hit (gravity, no floating) so the long vents can be marked; the way in and the way out read as the same sinkhole as the boss fight. Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-round-3-the-hole-and-the-cave-design.md; branch round-3-c from overnight-2026-10-23 0df35698; the cave's changes on branch flares-and-the-door of kai-denrei/stalheart-cave (commits 83e8f6a, 809f025), re-imported into below/ (BELOW.lock.json commit 809f0259). Nothing pushed.
outcome: The hole: the arena's breach was kept and spent, not sealed, at its sector's end, but BOTH WALLS' start caved in every live breach as a stray through killPortal(sp, 'exhausted'), the one reason a kept hole still took; sector-run keeps it as `nest` (state().sector.nest), begin leaves it out, and killPortal refuses a kept hole for every reason. The door in: the descent's look is the rim view while Isao's brief is read; then src/fx/hole-door.js dives over DESCENT.lookHold from the rim view up over the hole's axis and down it to 1.5 cells under the lip, the fov narrowing to 0.55, holds DESCENT.door.settle and the cave shows. The door out: as the cave posts its outcome the camera rises from under the lip, looking up, up the same axis to the rim view over 2.5 s, held there; the ending follows as before. In the cave (?stalheart=1 only): ISAO starts at the foot of the throat on the hole's axis over a rubble pile of the game's sizes under a down-facing sky disc and a dark rim torus, the camera tilting from the sky to the chase view over 2 s; RETURN TO THE SURFACE climbs the axis to the mouth over 2 s with a sky fade, then posts. The flares: gravity 9.8 m/s2 to 40 m/s, frozen 5 cm off the face at the first touch (clearance under 0.15 m, the normal from the clearance's gradient), no bounce or slide; the stuck stick lies on the surface, its light 0.3 m off it; the door's rubble is solid to them.
alternatives: confine's push-out as the flare's normal (the player's own call): by the blind branch's plug it pushes a point to the side wall and the flare read a normal into open air; the clearance field the same functions threshold, searched along its gradient, keeps every one of 1,242 dense drops within reach of rock.

The dive inside the first lookHold seconds, as before: it then sat under the lip in the dark for the 20 s of Isao's brief; the rim view holds through the brief and the dive leads straight into the cave.
The cave's new opening for the standalone game too: the spec leaves the cave's gameplay out; the door shows only in Stålheart's page.
evidence: Stalheart: npm test 305 programs (new test/hole-door.mjs; test/sector-run.mjs's nest asserts are red on the base), npm run check (below/'s lock and assets after the re-import), npm run architecture (td-tab 5,324 under 5,450), all green on the final tree; npm run build not run (out of time).

--arena on the decision-1 tree (snapshot): PASS, BOTH WALLS began, one more breach opened at cell 26595 through breachAt, the nest { cell 11659, open }, rubble caps 0 -> 0. Base --arena and --descent were green before the change.

--descent on the final tree: PASS; the hand-over fromCentre 1.33 cells, along -normal 1.00; the return's check passed at the rise's first pose (fromRim 1.52: the rim is 1.5 cells out, so a camera on the axis already reads under 2) and does not yet prove the rim view is reached; test/hole-door.mjs does (the rise ends at the rim pose, fromRim about 1 cell).

Cave: npm test 40 (flares: free fall at g to terminal, floors, a vertical wall stuck 5 cm off with no slide in 30 s, 35/50/70/85 degree slopes, 315 drops along the three passages all touching rock, 118 on a wall or the lean; door: start, tilt, climb, rubble), npm run check; a headless probe of ?stalheart=1 showed the sky up the throat at the start, the chase view after the tilt, the climb framed by the bowl's contours, no page errors. The cave's own browser suites were not run.
